entry.title: Woodland Hammock Hangout #2
entry.content:
This is the second post in a series about converting a shady back corner of the yard into a woodland.

Here we are covering how the first three steps in the to-do list went:

  1. Order mulch
  2. Pull up the grass carpet
  3. Put down the mulch

Ordering Mulch

The process was straightforward. I used Google Maps to see what mulch places were in my local area, and found out through their websites that I needed to figure out the amount of mulch in cubic yards (yd3). I measured the length and width of the woodland space then used a calculator on one of the vendor's websites to figure out how many cubic yards I would need, with a depth of 2 inches of mulch. The calculator told me 4yd3. I decided to triple it just to be safe, so I could use more mulch if needed and also have mulch for other areas I wanted to work on. This gave me a total of 12yd3 to order.

Then came the actual ordering part. I chose a vendor based on price - both the mulch and the delivery fees. Then I just had to call and put in my order for 12yd3 double grind brown mulch. It was delivered the next day! Now it was time to start removing all the greenery.

Pulling Up the Plants

I called it a grass carpet earlier, but there wasn't much grass. It was mostly Lady's Thumb with a few dandelions and other ground-hugging plants mixed in. I did not take the time to ID them all, I was on a rampage. The Lady's Thumb is really easy to pull up, progress was quick. It took about 5 days to clear the whole area, spending about 2 hours each morning. All the plants were tossed into the wheelbarrow as I pulled them out, and when the wheelbarrow was full, I would dump it in an area where it is okay for them to cold compost. This part of the project was the easiest but also tiring. I basically just crawled in the dirt ripping up plants while listening to music. You want to try to get every little green thing, which I didn't do perfectly. I fully expect to be weeding the area in a few weeks to get the stragglers. There are also alternatives out there to clearing the space, they just weren't options for me with the trees and my timeframe. I had first gotten some black tarps and put those down to smother the plants, it would have only taken a few weeks with the local climate. But I found out later that day that the trees could get damaged because their roots would be smothered with everything else and decided to just hand-clear the whole area.

Plant Pulling In Progress

Put Down the Mulch

After two days of pulling up plants, I started putting down mulch to cover the areas I had just cleared. I found out the hard way that a shovel is not the right tool for gathering mulch into the wheelbarrow, and went to the hardware store for a pitchfork. Much better!

All Pulled Up and Partially Mulched

This is how the rest of the week went. I would pull up plants for an hour or two, then put down mulch for an hour. For the trees, I learned you want to taper down to just about nothing right around their trunk, so the mulch doesn't keep the bark moist. The tradeoff here is that I am signed up for weeding the trees for a while.

Mulching Done

The Tree Stump Revealed

Coming Up

Next up we'll cover step 4, the hardest one in the to-do list: researching plants for the space!

[August 24, 2026]

entry.title: Woodland Hammock Hangout #1
entry.content:
This is the first post in a series about converting a shady back corner of the yard into a woodland.

The Idea

There are three trees that are a perfect distance from each other for hammock hanging. In the center of the triangle of trees is a stump. Other than the trees, there is a mix of boring grass and some other grass-like plants. This is it, it's just a grassy shady spot.

The goal is to replace the grass with mulch and put in a mix of shrubs, ferns, flowers, and maybe even exciting grass. These plants will provide interest throughout the seasons and act as a privacy screen. There is a stump in the center of the three trees that will also have flowers planted around it.

The Spot The Tree Stump

The To-Do List

Here is what we need to do to reach our dreams:

  1. Order mulch
  2. Pull up the grass carpet
  3. Put down the mulch
  4. Research plants that would work in that spot
  5. Get the plants
  6. Put the plants in the spot

Coming Up

In the next post, we'll cover how steps 1-3 went.

[August 17, 2026]
